## What the change does

It adds `src/receipts.ts` with one function, `receiptHeader(order)`. The function looks up the order's user with `findUser(order.userId)` and returns a line like `Order <id> for <name> <<email>>, <totalCents> cents`.

## Problems

**1. The user lookup can fail, and the code assumes it never does (blocking).**
`findUser` returns `User | undefined` (`src/users.ts:17-19`). The users module also exports `removeUser` (`src/users.ts:13-15`), which deletes a user from the map. Removing a user does nothing to their orders: `orders` in `src/orders.ts` is a separate array with no link back. So an order can easily outlive its user, and an order can also be placed with a `userId` that was never added.

The `!` after `findUser(order.userId)` only tells the compiler to stop checking. It does nothing at runtime. When the user is missing, `user` is `undefined`, and reading `user.name` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. Receipts for orders from deleted users would crash instead of being produced or failing with a clear error.

**2. No tests (should_fix).**
The change adds no tests at all, so neither the normal case nor the missing-user case is checked.

**Repository rules:** None are broken. The amount stays in integer cents (R2), nothing is logged (R1), and there is no SQL (R3).
